sources.quote: Inherited from Old Ruthenian мѣ́сцо (mě́sco), from Old East Slavic мѣстьце (městĭce), мѣстце (městce), probably influenced by Polish miejsce, from Proto-Slavic *městьce, from *město (“place, town”) + *-ьce. Equivalent to мі́сто (místo) + -це (-ce).

місце.text: Inherited from Old Ruthenian мѣ́сцо (mě́sco), from Old East Slavic мѣстьце (městĭce), мѣстце (městce), probably influenced by Polish miejsce, from Proto-Slavic *městьce, from *město (“place, town”) + *-ьce. Equivalent to мі́сто (místo) + -це (-ce).

червень.text: From Old East Slavic червьнъ (červĭnŭ, “June”), with -ень (-enʹ). Cognates include Belarusian чэрвень (červjenʹ, “June”), Czech červen, Polish czerwiec, and Bulgarian червен (červen, “July”). Related to a carmine-based red dye harvested from the larvae of certain insects, черве́ць (červécʹ, “carmine scales, cochineal”), at this time of year. Akin to Ukrainian червоний (červonyj, “red”).
